column2: Lord Stanley of Preston, the Governor General of Canada, became obsessed with ice hockey, a sport that originated from field hockey. He donated this trophy in 1892, and it became the prize for Canada's top amateur ice hockey club.

Uruguay has just hosted the first FIFA World Cup, achieving brilliant success. Although many European nations did not participate, it was still a great football feast. Most importantly, Uruguay defeated Argentina 4-2 in the final!
With a fiercely contested match, the first FA Cup began at the Kennington Oval in London. A surprising result saw Bolton Wanderers defeat the Royal Engineers 1-0 to win the championship.
We cannot encourage railway construction when we do not know how to build railways at all.
We cannot encourage industries that have not yet been invented.

The higher this value, the more violent uprisings will be.
Plurality refers to the level of awakening in our nation. Experiences, both successful and failed, remind the people to strive for that which is called freedom.
This term comes from the French word "revanche" (revenge). Revanchism refers to reclaiming lands that were once ours. Our people are willing to make greater sacrifices to achieve this goal.
Building a canal between the Baltic Sea and the North Sea will greatly benefit our shipping, and Kiel will become strategically significant.

Shipping to the Far East and Indian Ocean has always been a great problem, as we need to go around the Cape of Good Hope to reach there. But if the Suez Canal is built, it will greatly shorten our voyage to Asia, making it a modern engineering project of great significance.

The suggestion to build this great canal dates back to the time when this region was first discovered. The entire North and South American continent is narrowest here. With modern engineering, building a canal here can shorten the voyage from the Atlantic to the Pacific by several days.
Prestige gradually accumulates as you develop culture in your nation.
Industry rating represents your level of industrialization, determined by the number of factories and total production of goods in your nation.
Military refers to your military strength, determined by the size and equipment level of your army.

The eight nations with the highest ratings are called ?Y Great Powers?W, who can influence and control weaker nations. The eight slightly weaker nations are called ?Y Secondary Powers?W, who have the ability to colonize and at times challenge the Great Powers. The remaining nations are divided into ?Y Civilized Nations?W and ?Y Uncivilized Nations?W based on whether they are westernized.
Total number of soldiers fighting on this side
This is impossible and dishonorable — the enemy will not relent when you try to retreat
Cumulative deaths on this side at this stage
River crossings and beach landings are quite disadvantageous to the attacker
The defender's complete trench system is quite disadvantageous to the attacker
War intervention\nWe cannot join this side because:
Influence represents a ?Y Great Power?W's ability to influence the decisions of other nations.
Primary culture determines who are the first-class citizens of the nation
Accepted culture refers to cultures our nation can accept

It is a dark day for $COUNTRY$. The financial district of $CAPITAL$ is shocked by the bursting of the speculative bubble. Real estate prices rose rapidly over the past year and a half, and some analysts repeatedly warned that prices were at unnatural highs due to inflation, but bull market participants ignored all warnings. Voices within the government have called for stronger regulation of banks and currency, demanding an end to what they call "this dog-eat-dog failure of capitalism."
Balance the government budget, deregulate, and stabilize currency.
Our nation is affected by the stock market crash.

The great crash of the $CAPITAL$ stock market has evolved into a more severe form. Plunging depositor confidence in banks has led to bank runs, with people scrambling to withdraw their life savings. More and more banks and credit institutions are failing, creating a domino effect across the entire $COUNTRY_ADJ$ financial sector. Loan defaults and savings wiped out have quickly spread the crisis to other private industrial sectors. The manufacturing sector collapsed almost overnight, leading to widespread unemployment. The close economic ties of the Western world soon spread this crisis to other nations, and its effects echoed across the world, known as the $YEAR$ Great Depression.
This is just a short-term crisis, no one's fault.

Since $COUNTRY$ has no laws constraining private bank behavior, some private institutions are issuing their own currency. While there are arguments that people's hard-earned savings are too important to be left in the private sector, developments in one region of our nation are quite different — there, the presence of an overabundance of banking institutions allows people to freely choose where to deposit their money with banks they truly understand and trust.
This system could always collapse, what then?
As long as they're happy, I'm fine with it.

A newly formed railway company in our nation has issued internal stock to fund its growing operations, and is now seeking buyers and investors within the province. The company's CEO has approached local politicians, hoping they can assist with the company's stock listing, emphasizing that the extension of the provincial rail network is absolutely beneficial and should be supported. Some believe this would contradict the government's principle of neutrality toward private entrepreneurs, while others see it as an opportunity for development.
We will certainly lend a hand and support the excellent initiative of these private entrepreneurs.
I think the government should intervene as little as possible.

The government has been operating the central bank for some time now, and voices have emerged in economic debates calling for the minting power to be brought under strict government monopoly. Supporters say this is beneficial for economic stability, while opponents see it as an infringement on the principle of free trade.
Our government's central bank strictly monopolizes the minting of currency.

Buy Greenwood & Burns at 9.5, sell at 9.76! Altman & Sons at 8.12, sell! Sell!\n\nLocal businessmen in one of our provinces have formed a joint venture to establish a regional stock exchange primarily for commodity trade. This commercial activity will undoubtedly improve local production efficiency!
There is a stock exchange in this province, increasing local goods output.

A bank run occurred in this state today following reports that a local bank issued currency far exceeding its liquid assets. The situation has escalated to the national and parliamentary level, with opponents of the free banking system demanding stricter government regulation of banks, while industry interest groups and free trade lobbyists firmly oppose this.
The free banking system is the cornerstone of free trade.
The nation's economic policy must not be at the mercy of speculators' whims.

With basic needs met and prolonged low unemployment, our nation has entered a period of rapid economic development. High savings rates and an innovative people, combined with large investment banks and advanced economic methods, put us in an unprecedented excellent position to develop national industries and take our economy to new heights.
Distribute this wealth fairly and reasonably.
Our nation's economy is developing rapidly, thanks to investment banks and prolonged low unemployment.

After long-term debt-financed operations, a large company in one of our states has recently gone bankrupt. Local politicians have petitioned the government to support this company, claiming the downturn is only temporary and it can recover if given time to reorganize and restructure. While we can provide assistance, the armchair politicians in parliament have strongly criticized this idea, calling it an absurd infringement on the principles of free trade and government non-interference.
Obviously we must help this company through this difficult period.
We will not use government money to bail out a private company.

In $COUNTRY$, news of the so-called railway trust exposed by the regional antitrust committee is creating a stir. Local capitalists argue these claims are absurd, claiming they neither deliberately manipulated prices nor that price monopolies actually occurred. Many in the working class are very angry about this, feeling strongly that capital tycoons are benefiting by ruthlessly squeezing the impoverished. Dissolving this trust would set back local railway construction by several years, but not doing so might provoke the lower classes.
We must open this manipulated market and protect workers' interests at all costs.
Any form of infringement on free trade is unacceptable.
This determines how much tax the poor class must pay. Excessively heavy tax burdens may leave them without sufficient money to meet basic needs.
This determines how much tax the middle class must pay. Excessively high tax rates may leave them without sufficient money for daily necessities and career development.
This determines how much tax the rich class must pay. Excessively high taxes may leave them without sufficient money for consumption and factory investment.
Inventory expenditures for purchasing national reserves.
Government subsidies to factories and national cash reserves will help factories purchase materials and pay wages.
Tariffs are an additional tax on imported goods, the revenue goes to the national treasury. Negative tariffs mean your nationals receive subsidies when importing goods.
Income and expenditures generated by diplomacy or peace agreements.

When we look at all the injustice occurring in $COUNTRY$'s colonies, it's no surprise that in many places far from our coastlines, "$COUNTRY_ADJ$" has become synonymous with theft, robbery, and murder. Today, our message is clear and loud: $COUNTRY$! Stop colonialism! $COUNTRY_ADJ$ radicals have formed an Anti-Colonial League. Although ostensibly led by intellectuals advocating colonial independence, our secret police reports clearly indicate this league has close ties with international socialists.

The colonial rivalry between European nations for Africa and indeed the entire world is intensifying, and $COUNTRY$ is no exception. A $COUNTRY_ADJ$ colony has become a model of European colonial rule recognized worldwide in the past few years. The colonial experience gained from this colony has provided considerable assistance to $COUNTRY_ADJ$ scientific research and has brought international reputation in European parliaments and courts.

Although I absolutely respect my honorable patriotic colleagues in the opposition, I must question their motives in constantly raising the topic of colonial department expenditures. Colonialism is the cornerstone of government policy and deserves funding. With a sharp debate unfolding in the House of Lords, colonial policy has become a hot topic in $COUNTRY$ again. Opposition members advocate cutting the colonial department's budget, and they and most members of the House of Commons have launched a massive attack on the House of Lords, trying to persuade swing voters or those casually disposed to elections to support their policy.

An emerging corruption scandal in the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ colonies has shaken $CAPITAL$. A major newspaper published a report detailing a massive network of power-for-money trades, exchanging secret stock benefits for preferential treatment in colonial development and trade. Critics of government policy point to relatively low wages and meager funds allocated to the colonial department as decisive factors in this scandal, but the mainstream view within government circles seems to be that a culture of corruption in the private sector should bear responsibility for this poor state of the colonial department.
The government should take responsibility for its own shortcomings.
The colonial department is just affected by the general environment — it's the pervasive culture of corruption that should be blamed!

Our growing colonies have made $CAPITAL$ the center of an expanding economic and cultural empire. Every day, every hour, people from every conceivable corner of our world gather at our capital, flattering ministers, trading with merchants, engineers and industrialists, and meeting the fate that $CAPITAL$ bestows upon her visitors. Standing in the heart of $CAPITAL$, you can see a panorama of the entire world around you, hear every language and accent, and smell fragrant breezes from distant continents. In the annals of the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Empire, the year $YEAR$ will forever be remembered as the Golden Age of $CAPITAL$.

Discovering new lands also means discovering new diseases. One of our colonies has recently become known as a place particularly plagued by disease. It seems every traveler entering or leaving this colony always catches or brings back something extra and unpleasant: from typhoid to dysentery, various common or rare diseases. A report by a $COUNTRY_ADJ$ doctor permanently stationed in this colony states that a government-coordinated effort to drain local swamps and improve sanitation facilities would greatly benefit the colony, but it will obviously cost a lot of money.
Obviously we must help this colony change its current condition.

One of our colonies has achieved tremendous success in colonial activities and local commerce. The local government attributes the main factor to an ambitious land reform jointly implemented by $COUNTRY_ADJ$ capitalists and industrialists. According to reports, the colony is showing more attraction to immigrants, and the industrial sector is very satisfied with the report's content.
Cover up these reports — don't let the capitalists become arrogant!

An archaeological excavation in one of our colonies has yielded a large number of wonderful prehistoric artifacts, tentatively dated to the late Paleolithic period. This discovery will certainly provide new insights into our understanding of ancient life and local development history. The $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Archaeological Society has hailed this as a great breakthrough in $COUNTRY_ADJ$ archaeology. These ancient artifacts obviously need to be placed in a museum, but where is more appropriate? The Archaeological Society strongly demands they be placed in the $CAPITAL$ History Museum, while others suggest it's best to keep them in a local museum.
These things should be displayed near there.
These things can educate our next generation about humanity's shared heritage.

Something is wrong in one of our colonies. The local economy is controlled by several well-known $CAPITAL$ capitalists. One of their small enterprises, a local workshop, operates until early morning every day according to Western industrial standards, and the noise from the workshop keeps all nearby residents awake. This scene has become a symbol of the oppression and frustration that accompanies our colonial rule.
If the workshop needs to operate until early morning, why should we complain?
I think we can stop by the local chamber of commerce and talk to the lads about this...

Although Napoleon and his great army have been defeated, the ideological foundation of the French Revolution remains unshaken. In Germany, the old crown of the Holy Roman Empire has become meaningless, and ancient feudal contracts have been replaced by the Napoleonic Code. Everywhere in Europe, in coffeehouses and universities, ideas of liberalism, political reform, freedom of speech, and people's rights have replaced monarchical ideas, once again validating an ancient maxim: the trend of the world cannot be shifted by human will. National minorities long bound by royal power are gradually awakening and realizing that their destiny should be shaped by their own hands. Meanwhile, across the distant ocean, fertile Asia and Africa are beckoning. When the dust settles at Waterloo, Europe stands once again at the threshold of a new era — the Age of Liberalism.
It seems the liberal movement will grow in the coming years.

While our people are working in poorly managed fields, what has our government done to protect the starving farmers from this frightening potato blight that struck this year? Economic freedom allows imports of substitute foods, but existing privileges must obviously be preserved.\n\nLiberal sympathizers suddenly appeared everywhere and even in parliament, accusing our government of being unable to cope with the recent potato blight that struck one of our provinces. If the liberals grow stronger, they may well brew another revolution. We must consider sending troops to areas with liberal unrest.
Ban them in parliament, hopefully the countryside will stay calm.
Give them a voice in parliament — they're wasting their time anyway.

If we believe a local poet's account, $CAPITAL$'s streets are already full of police. A poetry collection publicly criticizing the nation's current situation, mentioning oppression and political regression, has sparked sympathy in one of our states. Liberals have become accustomed to protesting the old order in the streets, calling for liberalization of the political system and unity between compatriots at home and abroad, so much so that the call for national unity can be heard throughout $COUNTRY$. We must consider sending troops to areas with liberal unrest.
Set up an arsenal locally to deter them.
The appearance of a sizable military detachment has silenced the liberal unrest and revolutionary rumors that had been pervasive throughout $PROVINCENAME$.

The intense electoral campaign in $STATE$ has reached a boiling point, with a sharp debate on trade policy becoming a perfect battleground between supporters of free trade and protectionism, each trying to dominate the future of our merchants. Independent traders argue that goods must be able to pass borders freely, while protectionists claim our fragile industry urgently needs protection from dangerous foreign competitors. Which path will $COUNTRY$ choose: free trade or protectionism? The choice is yours.
We must protect trade against destructive external competition.
Some degree of trade protection for our manufacturers.
Let the debate develop freely — I don't care about the result!
Most importantly, let our merchants pass freely.
Never let personal freedom and commercial freedom disappear from the face of the earth!

The electoral debate in $STATE$ has lasted for several days. Not surprisingly, the issue that will decisively influence the election result is still the economy. We have many good economic theories, but voters want to see clear statements of government policy. How will the government ensure that every $COUNTRY_ADJ$ citizen gets their share of the cake in the coming term?
The doctrine of laissez-faire makes sense.
The doctrine of interventionism makes sense.
The doctrine of state capitalism makes sense.
The doctrine of planned economy makes sense.

The moral quality of our people has begun to decline. In the election campaign in $STATE$, this statement caused a stir among those debating religious diversity and religious tolerance. Many people have begun to question our nation's attitude toward religious beliefs, and there's no doubt these issues will influence future elections.
There is no such thing as gods!
People should have their own religious beliefs.
There is only one correct faith in this world!

In the disturbing atmosphere of the city hall, two debaters are arguing fiercely. The audience is stunned, for words like "immigrants," "minorities," and "cultural groups" are being tossed back and forth between the two. One argues that immigrants should integrate into the mainstream culture of their new homeland, while the other believes immigrants should preserve their cultural traditions and that $COUNTRY$ will grow stronger through the influx of different ways of thinking.
Their citizenship rights need to be restricted.
Military policy debate in local elections

Supporters and opponents of the military are lining up for the upcoming election. Militarists argue that the increasingly tense international situation and intensified military competition among the Great Powers fully justify maintaining a strong $COUNTRY_ADJ$ military. Others are not so sure and believe military spending in the government budget is already too high.
We are patriots, fighting for the fatherland!
Maintain constant vigilance toward external situations.
War is not a good thing after all.
War is a heinous thing, avoid it as much as possible.

Since $STATE$ increased sales and transit taxes on some important local goods, smuggling has emerged, which has become a focus of debate in the next general election. Various suggestions have been put forward.
Tariffs on these goods can be lowered, others raised.
We should lower tariff levels overall.

Foreign goods have driven several local $STATE$ products out of the market. Some citizens report increasing difficulty competing with these imports in the market. Local politicians have raised this topic in election debates.
The free trade system ensures our competitive advantage in the long run.
Essentially, free trade should be chosen.
The free trade system guarantees our success.
In some cases the local market really needs protection.
External competitors must always be kept out of the local market.

Merchants in $STATE$ are arguing with the Chancellor of the Exchequer about his plan to nationalize several private enterprises. The intensity of the discussion drew your attention, and you tried to calm both sides down.
I don't see where it needs to be nationalized.
You both have good points, but we will not nationalize it.
Let nature take its course — things have their own laws. No nationalization.
Good idea, but let me think about it first.
Debate on state capitalism system in $STATE$
The current number of targets is too large, we can't complete them. Other farmers stand quietly behind him. Their weather-beaten faces show the same judgment and anxiety as their spokesman.
Nonsense. Production targets cannot be changed.
If production targets prove wrong in the end, we will correct them.
Debate between localism and national intervention

A debate has suddenly broken out in the regional elections in $STATE$ over whether the government should intervene in local economic development. Supporters of state capitalism believe that in the long run, building a system that allows the government to continuously make direct investments will benefit local manufacturing development.
It will take time, but it will have effects.
A small amount of investment can be considered.
We must resist the idea of government interfering in economic development.
Debate on planning, economy, and freedom

Administrative departments in $STATE$ have come under fire for repeatedly implementing supportive government subsidies for local manufacturing. Opponents argue that "economic planners in our nation cannot predict consumer preferences, what goods will be scarce, or what goods will be in excess supply, so they cannot effectively coordinate material production," and the faltering central planning system has begun to exasperate the people of $STATE$.
Economic planners know what they're doing.
It's not a big deal, but we'll look into it.
They seem to have a point...

Some faithful believers in $STATE$ believe the state has not given them the attention they deserve for their hard work since the last election. They say that over the years, they have been committed to local community work in many ways: caring for the sick and orphans, helping those in need. They believe they deserve some support so they can continue helping others. And this has become a much-discussed topic in local elections.
Charity is good, but there isn't any.
Maybe we can take some measures to help them
Religious policy is highly controversial in $STATE$ local elections.

$COUNTRY_ADJ$ religious policy has become one of the many controversies in $STATE$ local elections. Although many believe the state should take a relatively cautious approach toward secularization, it is still opposed by many local faithful, who believe it will threaten long-standing religious privileges.
Secularization allows the state to remain neutral on moral issues

In the upcoming election debate, the religious issue is also on the agenda. As a religious leader in $STATE$, he opposes freedom of conversion, because the congregation under his jurisdiction is dwindling, and such changes are fundamentally endangering the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ moral framework.
Try to maintain an open viewpoint.
Although repugnant, we shouldn't have too many concerns
We will do our utmost — limiting religion is intolerable.

Using public funds to repair churches has become a hot topic in $STATE$ local elections. Supporters of the project argue that government support for religion can not only protect believers but also help local leaders resist revolutionary forces. However, opponents claim the state should not interfere in religious affairs that belong to the private sphere.
Could some funds be considered from the perspective of cultural importance?
This issue should fundamentally be left to the people to decide.
In principle, we must oppose this plan

The current influx of immigrants has created more demand for employment. Immigrant rights advocates demand that newly naturalized citizens enjoy the same rights as native-born citizens. This topic has become a hot issue in local elections.
They have no right to demand anything.
Why should they have the same rights?
We'll see what we can do.
The future is not easy, but we will do our best

A focus of debate between the two sides in local elections is that some $STATE$ residents feel unfairly treated by the state due to their origin. Liberals argue that the rights of immigrants and aliens should be respected. Opponents and public opinion claim that $COUNTRY_ADJ$ nationality is not something that can be obtained overnight, but requires a long process of years or even generations.
Limited citizenship until proven a loyal national
Limited citizenship should be the guiding principle of immigration policy
You know, equality is my dream

In $STATE$ local elections, the immigration issue has become a major topic. Liberals believe our society should extend voting rights to include immigrants. Others oppose it, perhaps out of fear of losing old rights rather than embracing equal voting rights as a belief. As the election approaches, debate on this issue in $STATE$ intensifies.
We must spare no effort to expand the scope of freedom
Only narrowly defined full citizenship is our goal.
We are basically in favor of full citizenship
Sadly! Full citizenship is not a good choice.

In the upcoming $STATE$ local elections, most debate revolves around $COUNTRY$'s defense policy. The nation has always taken a strong stance on defense policy, and this year seems no exception. Obviously militarist policy will be popular with voters, though some shifts in pre-election debate may reduce its influence.
No need to increase military spending
Mom says pistols are the devil's right hand
Military and defense debate in local elections

Your generals have begun to complain about the poor food soldiers receive and demand more money be spent on meals. Generals believe poor food reduces soldiers' combat effectiveness, while improving it requires better rations. This has become a top concern for many military families in $STATE$.
They need better food to fight better.
We'll see how much we can spend on their food.
This is not our first priority.
Maybe we should cut other things, like disarmament...

An important report shows that most soldiers' weapons are approaching breakdown and need to be inspected to see if they should be scrapped. Providing new weapons to soldiers may exceed the current military budget.
We might be able to do something about this
Their weapons need to be updated
Whole $STATE$ is concerned about "give peace a chance"

Anti-war views have some influence in $STATE$. Whoever can harness this influence in the upcoming election will brighten their electoral prospects. The only question is that pre-election debate will influence anti-war sentiment, which will largely affect their support for candidates.
The army needs guns, not gossip.
Perhaps violence is the answer to everything.

We, the younger generation of $COUNTRY$, gather to restore ancient freedoms. To make $COUNTRY$ the second Greece.\n\nInspired by the ideals of freedom, antiquity, and romanticism, as well as by the nation, radical students at the National University have formed a student association. They published a propaganda document calling for reform of electoral methods and advocating the revival of ancient and traditional freedoms of $COUNTRY$. Due to the rapid spread of these brave new ideas, the association quickly grew into a large mass organization on campus.
They must be allowed to express their views
Mainly, can we stop doing these pointless things?

When I read the works of Pericles of Athens, I'm always surprised by the advancement of ancient society. Looking back, thousands of years later, we are less free than people of that era.\n\nThe 19th century saw a renewed interest in ancient works. Many ancient societies, such as Rome and Greece, became sources of inspiration for emancipators, who searched ancient examples and experiences for common freedom traditions they wished to implement in modern society. Having some classical works reprinted by a local reform club was fashionable among the educated elite of $COUNTRY$.
Honestly, don't you have better things to do?
It's good to see the classics getting attention. But, like Socratic dialogues, is it for anyone?

He wept because he saw this suffering people refuse to breathe the ancient fresh air — the air of freedom and the birthright of $COUNTRY$'s free sons\n\nOne of our nation's most respected authors recently published a book. Critics call it the harshest critique of $COUNTRY$'s political system among books that passed through publication review. The book takes a radical view of liberalism and opposition to the old monarchy, while vigorously defending the rights of the people and the republic.
Best to ensure it's most popular locally?
Throughout all $COUNTRY$, such a voice must be allowed!

In some part of our nation, the Chamber of Commerce has filed angry protests with the local government, complaining that government economic intervention has harmed local trade and distorted the basic principles of the free market. Influenced by a series of Enlightenment works on free trade and non-interventionism from French physiocrats and Scottish Enlightenment thinkers, the Chamber of Commerce demands a change in government policy so they can operate independently in regulating trade as they see fit. If their demands are not met, they threaten to refer the matter to the national level.
Perhaps some minor adjustments to the local situation can be considered
I reject the political demands of the stubborn elite

A liberal professor from our university published an economics pamphlet. The pamphlet received significant attention from liberals in $COUNTRY$ and abroad. Although short, it is profound, particularly in its compelling arguments for the merits of the free market and laissez-faire. The author is often compared to David Ricardo and Adam Smith. We can condemn this as liberal propaganda that is erroneous in its viewpoints, but looking back, does it have any merit?
Obviously, we must be proud of this publication.
Of course, this is just propaganda to exploit the working class.

Members of the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Chartist Club have organized an assembly in some part of our nation, calling for the most basic voting rights for the broader populace in electoral law. Although ostensibly calm, the assembly could spiral out of control at any moment. Police are on standby, ready to intervene at any time, and some of them seem more eager than others.
Let the police control this assembly
As the revolutionary situation develops, let these blue boys go their own way.

The Corn Laws were a series of unpopular bills, one of the few representatives of British mercantilist policy, designed to protect British agriculture from cheap foreign grain, which naturally affected the ability of the British lower classes to obtain cheap food. Due to agricultural failures in 1845 and the subsequent Irish potato famine crisis, the Corn Laws were finally repealed in 1846. The repeal of this act marked Britain's entry into a prolonged period of free trade that lasted for much of the 19th century.
The Corn Laws, a series of unpopular regulations, have been repealed.

With the closure of the East India Company and the collapse of the Mughal Empire, Queen Victoria obtained the title of Empress of India in 1857. The person generally credited with proposing this title was the then Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli. With the establishment of the British Indian colonial government, the glorious rise of the sun never setting empire was unquestionable!

The Swedish Armored Ship Association was founded in 1912 for the purpose of raising funds to build coastal defense cruisers for the Swedish Navy. This project received tremendous support from the people, enabling the organization to present 15 million Swedish kronor to King Gustaf V for the construction of the Royal Swedish Navy's ship in 1915, less than a hundred days after its founding.
We have no loans to repay
Closest naval base is at ?Y$PROV$?W, still too far\n(Naval distance: need ?R$NEED$?W/?Y$CURR$?W)
Closest naval base is at ?Y$PROV$?W\n(Naval distance: need ?G$NEED$?W/?Y$CURR$?W)

Women's suffrage gradually gained recognition in Western society during the 19th century. This idea was first advocated by liberal thinkers, such as Mary Shelley and John Stuart Mill in England. This movement gradually developed over time and by the end of the century had grown into an independent ideology: feminism. Women's experiences in factories and other positions previously considered male-only during World War I became a key element in their struggle for the right to work, vote, and equality with men in other social spheres.
Our nation respects gender equality and allows women to vote in general elections.
Social expenditures are used to implement enacted social reforms. Their amount depends on our administrative efficiency. ?W

A massive military-industrial complex has emerged in the Ruhr industrial region, with some industrial magnates such as the Krupp family collaborating closely with the Prussian military and government, greatly enhancing Prussia's military and industrial capabilities. Voltaire once said Prussia was "an army with a state," and this description fits the Ruhr region perfectly.

The issue of women's suffrage has become a focal point at the anti-slavery conference held in $CAPITAL$. Among the delegates from various nations were some women, so an item on the agenda required that women delegates be denied the right to vote before the conference officially convened. The separate seating of male and female delegates also became a focus. Growing signs indicate that women of $COUNTRY$ and the entire Western world are striving to participate in various social activities.
This is clearly making something out of nothing
Excluding women from public activity is what's making something out of nothing

As the war drags on and more men are called to the battlefield, some important industrial sectors suggest temporarily employing women in factories. This policy has already proven effective in small-scale trials before — their work efficiency is no worse than men's, and they are better adapted to some of this work.
I Think the Major is a Feminist

My conclusion is that while some professions are indeed unsuitable for women, their presence in various workplaces will not pose any threat to social order whatsoever.\n\nA prominent military officer published an article in a major newspaper of $COUNTRY$. Women working was considered by many as the greatest mistake in recent years. The colonel supports women working in various positions and believes those who oppose it only prove that women working has become an unshakable fact
Working conditions for women definitely need regulation
This guy is definitely going nowhere in the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ army

The weather in $CAPITAL$ is terrible for us, everywhere is mud. The parade in the mud got its name from this.\n\nA committee on women's suffrage organized a parade this week, attracting about 3000 women of various professions, including textile workers, lawyers, artists and many others, gathering on the streets of $CAPITAL$ to demand freedom and voting rights. Considering the weather, this was an effort comparable to men's.
We must understand and support them
This pointless activity has gone on too long

Feminists campaigning in a bar in one of our provinces are becoming a laughingstock nationwide. Two women standing outside the bar with propaganda boards — appearing to be from the upper class but rather thin — were not only considered ridiculous but also disliked by some lower-class women, because these high-and-mighty people would only condescend to sophistry.
Never mind, this is freedom of speech
Perhaps people should listen more to these ladies' viewpoints?

Like many ideologies, early feminists had their own different opinions and perspectives. In Britain, the split between NUWSS and NSWRV is one example. Feminists in $COUNTRY$ are also divided due to their differing views.
We should support the conservative faction

Married women have no personal property. Law and marriage treat her property as one with her husband's. We want to change this — we want married women to have their rightful share of property and let the law distinguish between the property of both spouses.\n\nFeminists in $COUNTRY$ have begun a movement for property rights, striving for women's rights.
This human rights movement should be carried forward

We've traveled throughout the entire city. My girls and I spread out to every single block. It wasn't easy work, but it was an unforgettable happy time.\n\n$COUNTRY_ADJ$ feminists are distributing flyers extensively locally to gain public support, striving for their property rights, marriage rights, and voting rights.
I don't know what the local residents will think of them, I really don't know

Sir, if you're disturbed by the 156th student wearing a bonnet, I'd be happy to remove my headdress and sit quietly at the back of the classroom, but I will never voluntarily give up my class.\n\nAt $COUNTRY_ADJ$ University, controversy has arisen due to the presence of women. A woman was admitted to our institution of higher learning, which has greatly unsettled local conservatives.
Kick that show-off young lady out of the academy!
Would our learned professors really be displeased by this?

Although many women have enthusiastically tried to express themselves, it is very difficult.
- Simone de Beauvoir, The Second Sex

A famous $COUNTRY_ADJ$ suffragist published a feminist book, which has attracted the attention of women at home and abroad.

I call on you, sisters, to start writing letters — to members of parliament, to regional representatives, to your grandmothers, to anyone! These letters will show we have the same power as men!\n\n$COUNTRY_ADJ$ feminists have begun a letter-writing campaign. Their goal is for every member of parliament to receive a thousand letters per year until women's suffrage is passed. This campaign has already achieved considerable results.
I think this will have some influence in parliament
I think this will have considerable influence among the people

Four smashed windows, attempted arson, and attacks on two police officers... The officers were not physically injured, but their pride might not be so sure. "What on earth made you do this?"\n\nA radical $COUNTRY_ADJ$ feminist organization launched a violent march to get the government to pay attention to their issues. Local conservatives see this as damage to the national will and the beginning of the end of Western civilization.

A $COUNTRY_ADJ$ feminist imprisoned for violent marches has begun a two-week hunger strike in prison, protesting the unequal treatment of women in $COUNTRY_ADJ$. The protest has gained increasing attention and support under the slogan "Let Women Vote," and local politicians have begun discussing this. Now almost every newspaper on the streets is paying extreme attention to this.
I suggest the prison guards force-feed that madwoman

(This so-called) Cat and Mouse Act was passed in Britain in 1912 to avoid gaining public sympathy for suffragettes on hunger strike. The basic content is that a prisoner can be temporarily released for any serious health reason and taken back into custody after recovering, so the government doesn't have to bear the accusation of persecuting hunger strikers. A similar act was passed in one of our provinces to treat hunger strikers this way.
Pressure the central government to cancel this act

A research group composed of feminist supporters has gradually become well-known among international feminists over the past few years. The $COUNTRY_ADJ$ college where the research group is located has published several papers on philosophy, politics, and economics focusing on women at this time.
Never associate me with this disgraceful thing

When feminists in $COUNTRY$ achieved their goals, many other nations still lacked a democratic system that kept pace with the times and provided equality for everyone. Raising this point in international conferences to other nations shouldn't hurt, or it could be used to divert the attention of the domestic people.
I don't think they'll accept this calmly...
At least we're better than those people...

Never, we shall never go!\n\nOne of our states has become a stronghold for socialists in recent months since a labor union was formed from a local workshop. That union set an example for workers, and now unions have sprung up in every factory like mushrooms after rain. Some local notables have petitioned the central government to send troops to ban these unions.
We will never let the military attack the people they are supposed to protect
I think we should have enough manpower to send...
Those socialists have aggravated the already sharp labor-capital contradictions in the province and demand the formation of a national guard to escalate the situation
I don't recommend our people being protected by underworld
Anything that can stop the situation from worsening!

One of our factories has become the target of a non-violent but costly slowdown strike, and local socialists are believed to be the organizers behind it. The factory manager is considering dismissing all these slowdown participants.

Our nation is being increasingly impacted by Western modern civilization. In terms of modern technology, industry, and military, our long-standing traditional experience is almost useless. The influence of Western civilization has penetrated into every corner of the nation and into everyone's heart. Now our fate is in our own hands. The only way to stop the Western tide from spreading is to become like them.

Japanese history generally begins with Emperor Jimmu in 660 BC. Although the imperial line continues to this day, during the Edo period the emperor became a puppet, merely a spiritual symbol. Now, by restoring power to the emperor and beginning industrialization, establishing a constitution, and reforming the economy, Japan may be able to break free from the constraints of Western powers.

The tranquility of the early 19th century was broken in $YEAR$, as revolutions and liberal winds swept across the continent. The decrepit royal families could only huddle in corners trembling. The scenes of the French Revolution spread once again across the streets of Europe. Students and young people gathered under the banner of freedom for their dreams — for a free Europe
We will become free people like our fathers!

Those cowardly Lincoln supporters, when will they come face our Irish Brigade?\n\nWhile most Irish immigrants supported the Union during the Civil War, a small number joined the Confederacy, perhaps believing that the Confederate cause was as just as Ireland's independence from Britain.

Today our police crushed a strike launched by those troublemaking communists and revolutionaries, which greatly stimulated domestic communists and socialists. Those brainwashed local peasants have formed a fierce confrontation with tradition, order, and our government.
Let's hope this pointless thing doesn't happen again
But aren't those guys' hardships caused by the ruling class?

Workers at a machinery factory in our nation have gone on strike, pretending to be sick — either genuinely or feigning it — to attract public attention. One factory stopping production is bad enough, but worse is that large numbers of other workers have joined them, causing considerable impact on our industry. Perhaps we need to use some tough measures to stop them?
We have plenty of time, let's wait it out
Ban the newspapers reporting this news!

A newspaper as its name suggests has been published in $CAPITAL$ — the $CAPITAL$ Red Star, mainly published by the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Socialist Party. This newspaper reports on the lives of those in the lower strata deeply, and advocates workers' rights, union organization, democracy and freedom
I think they should report on the lower classes.
What a rag this is, used to wrap grilled fish?

Red flags fluttering in the wind, people flocked to watch this large march held by socialists, communists, union members and great workers. To commemorate the demonstrators killed in the 1886 Chicago Haymarket Massacre, such marches are held annually throughout $COUNTRY$. This year's march looks particularly successful, and there's no doubt this will increase the awakening and militancy of socialists.
Commemorating these destroyers and murderers in my country?
We will naturally support this act of strengthening international worker solidarity

There's a fox in the chicken coop,
A herd of cattle in the cornfield outside.
The union has collapsed,
Their proud red flag is torn.
—— Steve Earle

Capitalists in one of our provinces have begun using various methods to destroy unions, including hiring professional infiltrators to undermine union solidarity, in order to restore traditional order.
What a brilliant and delightful idea!
This violates the union's freedom act

When labor-capital conflicts escalated, capitalists in one of our provinces locked out factories and told workers this would continue until they stopped supporting unions. Local police supported this action and there were a series of clashes with workers around the factory premises.
We're already busy with trade, war, and production — I don't want to worry about worker organizations

The socialist party in one of our provinces has recently begun drastic changes under the leadership of their young and dynamic leader. Although they still support some basic socialist theories like emphasizing the role of the state, they have begun to embrace radical nationalism. The black flag flies in front of the (former) socialist party headquarters, making it clear they have evolved into a new political ideology: fascism.
Looks interesting, keep an eye on them.

Fascists in one of our provinces have formed a paramilitary organization loyal only to their leader — the Blackshirts, named for their black uniforms. This is a completely new attempt in $COUNTRY_ADJ$ politics, otherwise people fear other organizations will emulate them and form their own military organizations.
Try to suppress and ban them
Leave them alone, hope they don't come looking for trouble

Fascists have begun providing free food for the unemployed in the name of "protecting the vast workers of $COUNTRY_ADJ$ from the persecution of international capitalism." Many other parties, including the most powerful Liberal and Conservative Parties, criticize this as bribery of voters. However, the fascists turn a deaf ear to this.
They haven't broken the law, so the government shouldn't intervene
This is just deceiving the people — they must be stopped!

News has reached $CAPITAL$ that the Blackshirts, along with other fascist organizations, have begun marching on $CAPITAL$ from all over the country, aiming to seize power. The military has no intention of stopping them, as many senior officers are sympathetic to the fascists. This is a severe test for the young $COUNTRY_ADJ$ democratic government.
Forcefully send troops to stop them!
What Blackshirts, I'd have Whiteshirts too!

Veterans disappointed with the future of capitalism and liberal democratic policy have organized a paramilitary organization called the Freikorps, aiming to protect their homeland and people. They have begun political activities, threatening several liberal politicians and occupying a place in the people's hearts.
Prevent them from influencing the military

Fascists founded a newspaper called the "$COUNTRY_ADJ$ Dawn" in one province, covering everything from heaven to earth, and sharply criticizing communists, socialists, liberals, conservatives, foreigners, minorities, women, homosexuals, capitalists, the mentally ill, and criminals. It has gained popular support on many viewpoints.
I think its readership is mainly the lower classes
I think its readership is mainly the middle class

Serious political violence has broken out in one of our provinces. Fascists attacked the local liberal party headquarters yesterday, causing three deaths and multiple injuries. Now every night, fascists, socialists, and citizen guards fight in the streets, causing great panic among local residents. Many people demand increased public security budgets to control the situation.
Declare martial law locally and send troops.
Apologize to the Liberal Party on behalf of the state, for failing to protect its citizens

$COUNTRY_ADJ$ fascists have begun a campaign against foreigners, immigrants, and minorities. They launch hate attacks on minorities. Some cultural elites denounce this as excessive incitement and express support for minorities.

Fascists held a large march in the streets today to demonstrate their strength, wearing black and brown shirts, marching in military formation through the streets. Some cabinet members believe such uncontrolled military organizations are a potential threat and demand they be outlawed.
Since they want to march, let them
Outlaw them as an illegal organization

Word has it that fascists in one province plan an armed rebellion, setting up their headquarters in a beer hall, attempting to seize power locally. Our cabinet members are divided on how to handle this. Some believe local police can handle them, while others think troops need to be sent to suppress them. The latter, however, would gain the fascists more sympathy and support.
Decisively send troops to suppress them

Fascists in one of our provinces have organized an anti-socialist union, advocating what they call the "natural relationship between labor and capital." The union has greatly strengthened its power under the control of the fascist party. We can try to suppress them, but this may push workers toward the socialist union instead.
Outlaw them as an illegal organization

Carlism is a movement in Spain supporting traditionalism and legitimism. The Carlists were doubly threatened by liberalism in political ideology and economic relations, and were particularly hostile to those anti-clerical progressives, viewing them as mere Masonic puppets who hated the Church and tradition. They believed that only by accepting the rule of the legitimate heir, Prince Carlos, could order be restored.

France launched a military intervention against Mexico in 1861 over its refusal to repay loans. It supported Archduke Maximilian Ferdinand of Austria, later Maximilian I, as the emperor of the restored Mexican Empire. Although the empire lasted only three years, Maximilian gained some support from the Mexican conservative class to some extent. Supporting Maximilian's claim to the Mexican throne could return Mexico to a monarchy, but this would likely carry many risks.

The only problem with this arrest is that contrary to what the neighbor claims, the citizen was arrested on our side. The local police chief has demanded that his counterpart immediately release the $COUNTRY_ADJ$ citizen and make a formal apology to $COUNTRY$.
Regardless of their actions, this could be a justification for war.

The $CAPITAL$ Steamer, a small military steamer, exploded yesterday while docked at a foreign port — the explosion occurred on the starboard midsection and the ship subsequently sank. According to military intelligence, the explosion may have been caused by an overheated boiler. But the most widespread negative reports seized this opportunity and claimed the explosion was a premeditated and aggressive act by foreign forces. Our citizens are very angry about this event, and demands for blood repayment from foreigners can be heard in discussions on the road named after the ship in $CAPITAL$.
We cannot allow this treacherous barbarism to go unpunished!
This explosion was an accident — we cannot let mobs dictate foreign policy

Our ambassador to a major nation has sent a telegram, barely concealing disappointment over the failure to conclude a bilateral extradition treaty. Apparently, our ambassador has been repeatedly snubbed by the government of that nation. During negotiations, the other side dispatched ordinary civil servants rather than government decision-makers for talks. This kind of diplomacy has been going back and forth for two months.
Inform them of the potential consequences of continued non-cooperation
Write to thank them for this period and inform them of ending negotiations.

A regiment from our colony recently encountered a foreign army. According to military intelligence, the foreign army crossed the border along a little-known, non-short water route directly into our colony. The report further mentions that the army was conducting a regional geological survey when it encountered our patrol, but we cannot understand what their true intentions are. The hawks in our war cabinet see this as a direct attack on $COUNTRY$'s territorial integrity and demand the execution of what they call a plan to "provoke $COUNTRY_ADJ$ anger."
Someone invaded, then mobilize troops — interesting!
I don't believe this reported truth is worth going to war over

Intolerable — strong action must be considered!

Invoking our religious and military leaders, since foreigners arrived in our nation several days have passed, but soon they will be deported. In a recent high-level meeting, these Europeans who should be stopped from destructively exploiting our land were discussed.

Führer! The military high command has devised a cunning plan to expand $COUNTRY_ADJ$ Lebensraum through military conquest. By engineering a military incident with a neighboring nation, we can make our nation and world people believe our country has been attacked. Or spread terror and unprecedented enemy atrocities? We should...
Our academic world is in chaos, and will be rebuilt through a paradigm shift. Our prestige and research will be hindered, and this impact will persist.
Many in our academic community believe the current direction of academia is suffering from unnecessary prejudice. We should return to a more traditional image.

Cooperation between private industrial enterprises and the military in defense and war policy has led to the development of a very important network. This network relies on personal relationships and acquaintances, and there is inevitably some corruption. Therefore the best description of this network is the military-industrial complex. By deepening the goals and ambitions of these informal relationships in our academic world, we can increase military and industrial research, but at the cost of naval and cultural research.

Some say the best way for our nation to preempt strikes is by establishing naval academies. Many of our military and political elites have received naval education or served on merchant ships. For a maritime nation like ours, the importance of the navy cannot be underestimated. And with the promotion of political groups and backgrounds, we can ensure our naval technology will have great development, but at the cost of research in other fields.

In the past few years, our nation's avant-garde culture and thought have shouldered a arduous mission through our academic institutions. Through continuous efforts, this has become a step in the academic ladder — these radical new theorists are now sufficient to subvert our academic institutions to better meet their ideological needs. By supporting their cause, we can speed up cultural research, but it will be harmful to knowledge progress in other fields.

In the past few years, our nation has grown rapidly under the influence of ethnic groups who were educated in the same or similar upper-level business schools and corporations. Supported by these groups, we can ensure our academic focus is on what we care about: commerce and industry. However, this change will come at the cost of research in other fields.

In 1707, Frederick the Great obtained Neuchâtel through his mother's House of Orange-Nassau. The Principality of Neuchâtel then joined the Kingdom of Prussia in a personal union with the House of Hohenzollern. During the Napoleonic Wars, after being defeated by Napoleon, Prussia ceded Neuchâtel. In 1848, Neuchâtel abolished the monarchy and existed as a republic within the Swiss Confederation. In 1857, Prussia formally renounced Neuchâtel on equal terms.

For some time now, both government and capital in our nation have formed an intricate network based on personal relationships. John Brown's body lies a-mouldering in the grave, but his soul goes marching on. — "John Brown's Body," Union marching song\n\nJohn Brown, the famous hero of the abolitionist movement, was hanged in Charles City, Virginia, after his failed raid on the armory. Our "divided house" is tottering in the face of this strong wind from the South.

The Emancipation Proclamation is the collective name for two executive orders issued by President Abraham Lincoln during the American Civil War. It declared that all slaves in the Southern states would be freed. Issuing the Emancipation Proclamation will let the world know that in this war, nothing is more important than gaining freedom for all blacks.

With the smoke of Waterloo having cleared, the ideas of the French Revolution also faded away amid the joint suppression by European monarchs. After the suffering brought by the Napoleonic Wars, European nations reached an agreement at the Congress of Vienna to re-establish temporary peace on the troubled European continent. However, although the revolutionary fire has been extinguished, the ideas of human rights, nationalism, and liberalism remain vibrant. In this era of unprecedented scientific development, people will doubt things their ancestors had believed in for generations, and new doctrines will emerge. Across the distant ocean, fertile Asia and Africa — centers of the dark world — strive with all their might to secure a place in the concert of European powers. The Summer Palace is a luxurious garden located northwest of the imperial capital Beijing. Built between the late 18th and early 19th centuries as a vacation resort for Qing dynasty emperors, it was razed to the ground by the Anglo-French forces during the Second Opium War. This was a heavy blow to Chinese morale, and many in Europe, such as Victor Hugo, expressed great indignation at this barbaric act. Burning this palace will greatly damage Chinese morale.

The Old Summer Palace, known in China as the Yuanmingyuan, is a luxurious garden located northwest of the imperial capital Beijing. Built between the late 18th and early 19th centuries as a vacation resort for Qing dynasty emperors and a crystallization of Chinese architectural art. Today we learn that $FROMCOUNTRY_ADJ$ forces occupying Beijing have burned down the Summer Palace. The entire nation is devastated by this barbaric act.

Since the Qing dynasty, power in China has been concentrated in the hands of the Manchus, and Qing emperors have always treated Manchus and Hans differently. In the 1860s, Empress Dowager Cixi handed military power to Han Chinese Zeng Guofan to suppress the Taiping Rebellion, ending full Manchu control of China. Ending Manchu dominance can speed up our modernization.

Muhammad Ali, an Albanian born in Macedonia under Turkish rule, was the second-in-command of an Albanian regiment sent to Egypt to oversee the French withdrawal in the early 19th century. After the French troops withdrew from Egypt, he emerged victorious from a political struggle and was appointed governor of Egypt by the Turkish Sultan. During his reign, he carried out various reforms, both praised and criticized, targeting the Egyptian upper class to modernize Egypt into a European-style state. These included establishing a naval shipyard in Alexandria, placing most farmland under government management, and sending missions to Europe to learn advanced Western technology. Promoting these reforms can push Egypt further toward modern society.
We have implemented the Muhammad Ali Reforms, and our technology has benefited as a result.

Reconstruction is a compound term encompassing a series of political changes, laws, decrees, constitutional amendments, and presidential orders. After the American Civil War, in order to reintegrate the Confederate states into the nation. The policy focused primarily on abolishing slavery, suppressing Southern nationalism and revanchism, and endorsing the Thirteenth Amendment passed by the Southern states. The amendment was finally abolished after a compromise between the two sides in 1877, and federal troops finally withdrew from the South. Confederate flags were trampled in the ruins of Savannah and Richmond. It's time to begin rebuilding our nation.

The KKK is a secret lynching group, known for its iconic symbols like burning crosses, white masks and robes. It was founded to oppose the Republican Party's Reconstruction principles, dedicated to preserving white supremacy in the former Confederate states. The KKK stopped at nothing to achieve its goals, with direct violence against Southern Republicans and blacks being the least of it. In President Ulysses S. Grant's first term, the federal government abolished the KKK through the Enforcement Act of 1871. Today we receive news that burning crosses have been seen, flames shooting into the warm, dark night sky of the South.

Serfdom — unfree farm laborers bound to the noble's land, effectively a form of feudal slavery — has existed in Russia in various forms since the Kievan Rus' period in the 11th century. Although the system underwent several reforms and transformations over the centuries, the first step toward complete abolition was only taken in the 1810s, when it was abolished in Russian Courland, Estonia, and Livonia. It was not until the reign of Tsar Alexander II that serfdom was abolished throughout Russia in the 1861 agricultural reform — he feared that otherwise Russian peasants would seek liberation through a thorough revolution.

Tanzimat (reorganization) in Turkish, refers to a series of reform measures enacted by the Ottoman government in the second half of the 19th century to counter the rising nationalist tide among the empire's vast and diverse minorities. The reformists aimed to integrate diverse populations under the common banner of "Ottomanism," reforming the Ottoman government as an alternative for the many radical minorities in the nation seeking to establish nation-states based on a single ethnicity, and allowing increased minority representation and autonomy in government. The Tanzimat reforms ultimately failed to prevent the decline of the Ottoman government, though it can be said they at least delayed the decline.

The Civil Guard (Spanish: La Guardia Civil) is Spain's gendarmerie, founded during the reign of Queen Isabella II, after the liberal victory in the Carlist Wars, to suppress Carlist nostalgia lingering in the countryside. The Civil Guard is a mixture of police and military force, operating at the national level, and has survived to the present day.
This gendarmerie is the pride of the nation.

The Foreign Legion (French: Légion étrangère) is a military unit of the French army, unique in that it recruits new soldiers regardless of nationality and personal background. Founded in the early 1830s, the regiment did not yet have the long tradition it enjoys today until it served alongside other forces in the Spanish Carlist Wars, French intervention in Mexico, Cameroonian campaigns, the Franco-Prussian War, and in fact, in almost every conflict involving France up to modern times. Young people fleeing personal tragedy, oppression, debt, or past crimes might join the French Foreign Legion, embarking on a journey of redemption in the deserts of French Algeria — a scene that has since become one of the most iconic and enduring images of the 19th century. Promote the legion, let new recruits rally to our banner.
Our army is world-famous, and the Foreign Legion's long tradition deserves much of the credit.

The Dar al-Funun was the first modern university-style institution established in Persia, founded in 1861 by Amir Kabir, who later became the Grand Vizier of Nasir al-Din Shah of the Qajar dynasty. It was a modern polytechnic institute dedicated to teaching medical skills, natural sciences, and military technology to children of the Persian upper class. By establishing such a fine institution, let's give our young people a taste of the modern world!

During the War of the Triple Alliance, when Paraguayan forces invaded Brazil's Mato Grosso province, Emperor Pedro II of Brazil, exasperated by the incompetence of the Brazilian army, asked to be allowed to go to the front alone. When both the cabinet and the national congress rejected his wish, Pedro threatened to abdicate and join as a volunteer, reportedly saying "If they can stop me from going as emperor, then they cannot stop me from abdicating and going as a fatherland volunteer." Of course, the cabinet had no choice. Later, Brazilians who volunteered during the war were called "fatherland volunteers" in memory of Pedro's words. Like Pedro, this nation will follow your leadership forward.

Law No. 1420 on Elementary Education was passed in 1884 during the presidency of Julio Argentino Roca of Argentina. The law established the nation's first free, compulsory, national, and secular education system. Despite the law's secular tendencies causing conflict between the Catholic Church and the Argentine government, it can be considered a milestone in Argentine education.

Denmark had been an absolute monarchy since 1660. On June 5, 1849, King Frederick VII signed a document called the "Constitution of Denmark," establishing Denmark's constitution. The signing of this constitution, which limited the monarch's power, was a new thing that Frederick's predecessors had tried hard to avoid, initiated during the unification of Denmark, following the First Schleswig War. The constitution marked Denmark's transition from absolutism to constitutional monarchy. Give our people a constitution!

"Die Stem van Suid-Afrika" (The Voice of South Africa) did not officially become South Africa's national anthem until 1957, but it had been the unofficial anthem for a long time before. The lyrics were originally written by C.J. Langenhoven in 1918 as a hymn, and set to music by Marthinus Lourens de Villiers in 1921. "Die Stem" was frequently broadcast on the South African Broadcasting Corporation, and aired together with "God Save the King" at the end of each broadcasting day. With "Die Stem," give our young nation a fitting anthem!

The British Broadcasting Corporation, Britain's public service broadcasting network and later television network, was founded on October 18, 1922, as the "British Broadcasting Company." The company was initially formed by a consortium of six telecommunications companies, and sent its first broadcast from London's 2LO station on November 14, 1922. From the BBC, let "nations live side by side in peace."

Soviet Narodnykh Kommissarov, Russian for "Council of People's Commissars," was the highest government authority in Soviet Russia, functioning according to custom from the 1918 Russian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic Constituent Assembly. The Council of People's Commissars (officially) was responsible to the Soviet Assembly, and during its recess, had the power to issue laws and decrees.

The mission was led by General Charles Canron, who later became Minister of War in the Brizon government in 1898. We will dispatch a military mission to Japan, which will definitely strengthen relations between the two nations.

Support Schwabing and let it bring us glory.

Grunderzeit refers to the period between the 1840s and the mid-1870s, when Germany and Eastern Europe, particularly Vienna, experienced rapid economic modernization and industrialization. This period is famous for its architectural style, inspired by neo-Gothic architecture and new architectural styles brought by the Industrial Revolution, along with the accompanying political trend of liberalism. Vienna will support these trends during this period and watch itself prosper.

In 1840, French Prime Minister Adolphe Thiers declared the Rhine as France's eastern border, which Germans considered an aggression against Prussia's territories on the west bank of the Rhine, igniting the Rhine Crisis. In response, the patriotic poet and merchant Max Schneckenburger created a patriotic poem entitled "The Fatherland's Watchful Care," in which the line "watchfully guarding the Rhine" implied that Germany would defend the Rhine against any (French) invader. The poem was set to music in 1854 and became widely popular during the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–1871.

Countless Chinese converts to Christianity were also killed by them. The Qing government showed indifference, and there were even reports that the Qing authorities tacitly approved of the thugs' actions.

The Boxers, commonly known as the "Boxers" or "Boxer rebels," were a Chinese organization dedicated to regaining national sovereignty lost to imperialism. The Boxers have appeared in several provinces of the Great Qing that have been encroached upon by foreigners. Support this movement and let us pray they can end the foreign influence on the Great Qing.

The monument broke ground in 1871 and was completed in 1883. It was built to commemorate the founding of the German Empire after the Franco-Prussian War. The "Era of Princes' Strife" (Zemene Mesafint) in Ethiopian history began in 1769 and ended with the ascension of Tewodros II in 1855. During this period, Ethiopia was torn apart by political strife, and the royal family could only occupy a symbolic position. After Tewodros II was crowned "Negusa Nagast" (King of Kings), the era of princes' strife came to an end, opening the modern imperial era of Ethiopia. Is it time to hold a coronation?

In 1843, the first parliament of modern Greece was established, and they forced King Otto to agree to issue a constitution only after the third revolution in September of that year. The establishment of the Greek Parliament not only symbolized Greece's transition to a constitutional monarchy, but also represented Greece's first step toward democracy since ancient times.

The Palais Garnier was the main venue for the Paris Opera from its official opening in 1875 until 1989. Designed by Charles Garnier, it features a neo-Baroque style. This opera house was celebrated as a masterpiece of modern architecture in its era and was imitated by the Western world. The Palais Garnier also inspired Gaston Leroux's classic novel "The Phantom of the Opera."

As one of the iconic police departments of this era, it was frequently mentioned in the works of Jules Verne and Arthur Conan Doyle. Scotland Yard can help us solve a crime or two.
London's police force, Scotland Yard, often plays the role of Sherlock Holmes' partner in literary works.

Through his experiences, Dunant began calling for the establishment of an international organization dedicated to handling war wounds, while conducting extensive lecture tours in Switzerland. Against this background, the Swiss Congress held an international conference in Geneva in 1864 to draft international laws governing the conduct of war.

The Folk School Reform, this "people's school" reform, was a law passed by Sweden in 1842, proposing compulsory education for Swedish children in several basic subjects. The folk school ensured the foundation of the Swedish education system until the early 1970s, when it was gradually abolished due to its favoring of ignorance and rudimentary principles.
An effective and modern compulsory education system that educates your young people in several basic subjects.

Edgardo Mortara was born in Bologna in 1851 to a Jewish family. During an illness in 1857, a Catholic maid of the Mortara family baptized him out of fear that he would go to hell if he died as a non-Christian. Based on the baptism, the Papal States police took Edgardo from his home and raised him as a Roman Catholic, even though the Papal States' law prohibited non-Christian children from becoming Christians. This incident, or rather an abduction, caused an international stir, with Napoleon III, Emperor Franz Joseph, and the London Times all protesting. Mortara himself eventually became a Catholic priest and restored contact with his mother and siblings for the rest of his life.

In 1868, Pope Pius IX convened the 20th Ecumenical Council of the Roman Catholic Church. The council discussed modern ideologies brought by liberalism, rationalism, and materialism, promoting the definition of Catholic doctrine. Although the council reduced Rome's interests due to the newly formed Kingdom of Italy, it also left a lasting Catholic theological concept in the formal doctrine of papal infallibility.

Tsar Alexander III issued the Manifesto on Unshakable Autocracy on April 29, 1881 (Julian calendar), about two months after his father Alexander II was assassinated by Nikolai Rysakov of the terrorist organization "Will of the People." The manifesto fiercely rejected the various liberal reform ideas held by his father, instead advocating for Russia's traditional and unshakable autocracy.

The Ems Ukaz was issued by Tsar Alexander II in 1876. In addition to reprinting old documents, it banned the use of the Ukrainian alphabet in all printed materials, contemptuously referring to it as a "minor Russian dialect." The ukaz was named after Bad Ems, a German spa resort, where the Tsar was staying when he issued it.
